title: ChatGPT now
builds working
tools in chat
slides.subtitle: Since 7 October, answers can include calculators, forms and charts. Here are five tools we would ask it for first, and the catch.

slides.label: A quote calculator
slides.detail: Give it your hourly rate, materials markup and VAT, and ask for a calculator with boxes for hours and materials. Change the inputs per job instead of redoing the sum each time.
slides.start: Ask: 'Build a quote calculator: hours x my rate, materials plus 15% markup, then 20% VAT.'

slides.label: A break-even calculator
slides.detail: Enter your fixed costs, your price and your cost per sale. It shows how many sales you need before you make a penny. Slide the price up and down and watch the number move.
slides.start: Ask: 'Build a break-even calculator with sliders for price and monthly fixed costs.'

slides.label: A supplier quote comparison
slides.detail: Paste in three supplier quotes and ask for a side-by-side table with the total cost over twelve months, including delivery and any minimum order. The cheapest headline price is not always the cheapest.
slides.start: Ask: 'Compare these three quotes over 12 months, including delivery. Flag anything missing.'

slides.label: A 12-week cash chart
slides.detail: Type in expected money in and bills going out each week and ask for a chart. Weeks where the line dips below zero are the ones to sort out now, not on the day.
slides.start: Ask: 'Chart my cash week by week for 12 weeks from these inputs, and flag any dip below zero.'

slides.label: An enquiry form that asks your questions
slides.detail: Every new enquiry gets the same five questions from you. Ask for a form that captures them, so you can fill it in on the call and read back a clean summary at the end.
slides.start: Ask: 'Build a form for new enquiries: name, job type, address, timing, budget. Then summarise it.'

slides.label: Then check the sum before you trust it
slides.detail: Commentators have already warned that a tool built on the spot can still get the maths wrong. Run a job you have already priced through it. If the answer differs from yours, fix the prompt. Keep customer details out.
slides.start: Test every new tool on one job where you already know the right answer.

title: Ask it for the tool.
Check the sum.
slides.body: This is the list we would try first, tested against a job we had already priced. Which plans get it, and exactly how it behaves, is still settling, so try it on yours.
slides.cta: Which sum do you redo most often that a little tool like this could do for you?
